newsitem.title: USA: IRS wants muni mart input on new US tax provisions.
newsitem.headline: IRS wants muni mart input on new US tax provisions.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service wants to know if municipal bond market participants want help implementing key sections of Congress' new tax bill, an IRS official told bond lawyers Friday.
President Clinton is expected to sign the tax and balanced budget package later this week.

The far-reaching plan includes several provisions sought by the muni market, particularly a repeal of the $150 million cap on the amount of bonds that non-hospital 501(c)(3) groups can have outstanding.
"Any time we have a new tax act, people in IRS and Treasury develop an implementation plan," said Michael Bailey, counsel to IRS' assistant chief counsel for financial institutions and products.

"If you have thoughts on issues that need to be (addressed), it would be helpful to know that as soon as possible," said Bailey at a meeting of the American Bar Association's committee on tax exempt financing here.
Bailey said the U.S. Treasury Deptartment took a "first glance" at some of the more significant provisions for munis, including the $150 million cap repeal.
It decided that there is no "urgent need" for a new rule on how to implement muni provisions, he said.
"Maybe that's an incorrect perception," Bailey said. "If you feel there are questions that need to be resolved promptly, it would be helpful for us to know that."

One audience participant said he wants guidance on whether the provision repealing the $150 million cap applies to 501(c)(3) organizations involved in mergers or consolidations before the effective date of the new tax law.
"We realize there are a few significant questions that need to be answered," Bailey said.
He said IRS would try to respond in a revenue ruling or other quick procedure, rather than taking the time to develop a regulation.
"I'm throwing out the idea," Bailey said. The idea is to "do it in some discrete way with a rifle shot or revenue ruling or something else," he said.
